name: Ceftriaxone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Ceftriaxone is cleared by both the kidneys (33% to 67% unchanged) and bile, so its kinetics change little with kidney impairment. The US label needs no dose change up to 2 g per day in kidney impairment, and hemodialysis does not remove it. Encephalopathy, seizures and nonconvulsive status epilepticus have been reported in severe kidney impairment, and in a few dialysis patients elimination was markedly reduced.

bands.recommendation: No dose change up to 2 g per day (label).
No dose change up to 2 g per day (label).

No dose change up to 2 g per day, but neurologic adverse reactions (encephalopathy, seizures, myoclonus, nonconvulsive status epilepticus) have been reported in severe kidney impairment; the label asks for appropriate dose adjustment there without giving one. Caution with both severe kidney and liver disease (label).

hd.text: No supplemental dose: not removed to any significant extent by hemodialysis (label). Dose up to 2 g per day; elimination was markedly reduced in 6 of 26 dialysis patients in the label's PK data, so watch for neurologic toxicity.

pd.text: Not reduced by peritoneal dialysis (label). For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): intraperitoneal intermittent 1,000 mg daily; no data for continuous dosing.

crrt.text: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): no change in CVVH, CVVHD or CVVHDF; clearance on CVVH was similar to normal kidney function.

dialyzable: No: not removed to any significant extent by hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis (label). Protein binding 85% to 95%.
monitoring: Neurologic status in severe kidney impairment; gallbladder sludge or stones and kidney precipitation (symptomatic ceftriaxone-calcium precipitates); hemolytic anemia; prothrombin time in patients at risk (label).

pediatric.approved_ages: Children, including neonates, except premature neonates up to 41 weeks postmenstrual age, hyperbilirubinemic neonates, and neonates needing IV calcium (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Serious infections other than meningitis: 50 to 75 mg/kg/day once daily or divided every 12 hours (maximum 2 g/day). Meningitis: 100 mg/kg/day (maximum 4 g/day). Acute otitis media: 50 mg/kg IM once (maximum 1 g) (label).
